name: mwnn-kanban
description: An in-editor MWNN Kanban board. No usage, board, or time data is transmitted.

commands.title: Populate Agent CLI Models and Thinking Levels

mwnn-kanban.confirmCardDeletion.description: Ask for confirmation before deleting a card.

mwnn-kanban.boardFolder.description: Workspace-relative folder where the Kanban board files are stored.

mwnn-kanban.defaultReadyReverseWip.description: Minimum number of defined cards the Ready column should keep available by default.

mwnn-kanban.enableRunWithAI.description: Enable AI-assisted board actions when those commands are available.

mwnn-kanban.chatProviderCommands.description: Override the VS Code command used to open each AI chat extension for 'Run with AI' handoff. Keys: copilot, codex, claude-code. Leave empty to use the built-in defaults.

enumDescriptions: Ask whether to use a VS Code chat extension or a local agent CLI.
Run the loop through an installed VS Code AI chat extension.
Run the loop with GitHub Copilot CLI.
Run the loop with OpenAI Codex CLI.
Run the loop with Anthropic Claude Code CLI.
Run the loop with Cursor Agent CLI.
mwnn-kanban.aiLoopProvider.description: AI execution channel or provider used by the AI board loop.

mwnn-kanban.aiLoopReviewFreshDefinitions.description: Pause cards the AI board loop has just defined in the Ready column until the next run, so a human can review the fresh Description and Acceptance criteria first. When off, the loop continues and implements freshly defined cards in the same run.

mwnn-kanban.aiLoopVerifyCards.description: Let the AI board loop verify cards in the Verify column and move them to Done when every acceptance criterion is confirmed, handing anything it cannot confirm back to a human. When off, every card reaching Verify is assigned to a human for verification.

mwnn-kanban.aiLoopCliFallbackEnabled.description: Let the AI board loop continue automatically on another agent CLI when the active CLI reports exhausted credits or a spent usage/session limit. The interrupted card stage is retried with the replacement CLI against the current card and workspace state. When off, an exhausted CLI stops the loop exactly as before.

mwnn-kanban.aiLoopCliFallbackOrder.markdownDescription: Ordered agent CLIs the AI board loop falls back to when `#mwnn-kanban.aiLoopCliFallbackEnabled#` is on and the active CLI runs out of credits. Duplicates, the exhausted CLI itself, and CLIs whose executable is unavailable are skipped. Each CLI is tried at most once per loop run; when none is left, the loop pauses without advancing the interrupted card.

mwnn-kanban.aiLoopModelEscalationEnabled.markdownDescription: Let the AI board loop retry a card stage on a stronger model when the attempt reports `STATUS: BLOCKED` or exits without the stage's required completion evidence. The retry uses the next model in `#mwnn-kanban.aiLoopModelEscalationLadder#` for the CLI that is running, against the same card and workspace state. Spent credits, authentication failures, network failures, cancellation, and a model name the CLI rejects never escalate, because a stronger model cannot fix any of them. An escalation never advances the card by itself: the stronger model still has to satisfy the same completion evidence rules. When off, an inconclusive attempt stops the card exactly as before.

mwnn-kanban.aiLoopModelEscalationLadder.markdownDescription: Ordered model names the AI board loop escalates through for each agent CLI when `#mwnn-kanban.aiLoopModelEscalationEnabled#` is on, cheapest first. After an inconclusive attempt the loop retries the same stage on the next entry above the model that just ran. Each entry is tried at most once per card per loop run, so a card walks the ladder once and then stops; when the ladder runs out, the original failure stands. Model names are CLI-specific and are passed through unchanged, so spell each one the way that CLI accepts it. Leave a CLI out to never escalate on it.

copilot.description: Models to escalate through for GitHub Copilot CLI, weakest first, as that CLI spells them. The loop moves to the next entry after an inconclusive attempt.

codex.description: Models to escalate through for OpenAI Codex CLI, weakest first, as that CLI spells them. The loop moves to the next entry after an inconclusive attempt.

claude-code.description: Models to escalate through for Anthropic Claude Code CLI, weakest first, as that CLI spells them. The loop moves to the next entry after an inconclusive attempt.

cursor.description: Models to escalate through for Cursor Agent CLI, weakest first, as that CLI spells them. The loop moves to the next entry after an inconclusive attempt.

mwnn-kanban.aiLoopModelEscalationOverrid.markdownDescription: Let model escalation replace a model a card names for the active CLI in its own `preferredModel.<provider>`. Off by default: a card-level model is an explicit choice for that card's work, so the loop leaves it alone and reports the failure instead of escalating. Turn this on to let `#mwnn-kanban.aiLoopModelEscalationLadder#` override a card's own model after an inconclusive attempt; cards that name no model are escalated either way.

mwnn-kanban.aiLoopMaxDispatches.markdownDescription: Maximum number of agent handoffs a single AI board loop run may dispatch before it stops on its own. Every launched handoff counts, including credit-fallback replacements and model-escalation retries. `0` (the default) disables the cap: run length and behavior are unchanged. When the cap is reached the loop stops *before* starting the next handoff, so no CLI is left running and the in-flight card is not advanced; the reason is recorded in that card's Activity. This is a count of dispatches, not a spend limit — the extension has no price table and never estimates cost. Any monetary or token figure in the end-of-run report is a line the CLI printed itself, quoted and attributed to that CLI.

mwnn-kanban.agentCliPaths.description: Optional executable path overrides for the agent CLIs used by 'Run Card with AI' and the AI board loop. Values are executable paths only (not shell command lines), and paths containing spaces are supported.

copilot.description: Path to either the standalone GitHub Copilot CLI executable or the GitHub CLI (gh) executable. The modern built-in 'gh copilot' passthrough is supported; the retired github/gh-copilot suggestion/explanation extension is not.

codex.description: Path to the OpenAI Codex CLI executable.

claude-code.description: Path to the Anthropic Claude Code CLI executable.

cursor.description: Path to the Cursor Agent CLI executable.

mwnn-kanban.defineUseJev.markdownDescription: When a card is defined with AI, ask TypeSafe's Jev model to judge the card's difficulty and pick each agent CLI's `preferredModel.<provider>` and `thinkingLevel.<provider>` from the names in `#mwnn-kanban.agentCliModels#` and `#mwnn-kanban.agentCliThinkingLevels#`. Jev is used only when the `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` environment variable is set; otherwise, or if Jev fails or times out, the defining agent chooses from the same names and the definition proceeds normally.

mwnn-kanban.defineOverwriteRunSettings.markdownDescription: Let card definition replace a model or thinking level already set on the card. Off by default, so a model or level someone chose for a card is kept and only providers the card names nothing for are filled in.

mwnn-kanban.agentCliModels.markdownDescription: Model names for each agent CLI used by 'Run Card with AI' and the AI board loop. The **first** entry for a CLI is the model that CLI runs when a card names no model for that CLI; the remaining entries are that CLI's other known models, offered when choosing a card's model. Model names are CLI-specific and are passed through to the CLI unchanged, so spell each one the way that CLI accepts it. Leave a CLI out to let it run its own default model.

copilot.description: Model names GitHub Copilot CLI accepts, as it spells them. The first entry is the default used when a card names no preferred model.

codex.description: Model names OpenAI Codex CLI accepts, as it spells them. The first entry is the default used when a card names no preferred model.

claude-code.description: Model names Anthropic Claude Code CLI accepts, as it spells them. The first entry is the default used when a card names no preferred model.

cursor.description: Model names Cursor Agent CLI accepts, as it spells them. The first entry is the default used when a card names no preferred model.

mwnn-kanban.agentCliStageModels.markdownDescription: Model name to use for each AI board loop stage, overriding `#mwnn-kanban.agentCliModels#` for that stage only. Useful when the short reasoning stages do not need the model the workspace runs implementation on. The model a card names for the active CLI still wins, then this setting, then the first entry in `#mwnn-kanban.agentCliModels#` for the active CLI, then whatever model that CLI runs by default. Model names are CLI-specific and are passed through unchanged, so spell each one the way the CLI you run accepts it. Leave a stage out to fall back to the workspace default; leave the whole setting empty for unchanged behavior.

definition.description: Model for the definition stage, which fills in a card's Description and acceptance criteria. A short reasoning task that does not edit the workspace.

triage.description: Model for the triage stage, which decides whether a card is doable as written. A short reasoning task that does not edit the workspace.

implementation.description: Model for the implementation stage, which does the card's actual work in the workspace. Also used by the Run Card with AI command.

verification.description: Model for the verification stage, which checks a finished card's acceptance evidence against the workspace.

mwnn-kanban.agentCliThinkingLevels.markdownDescription: Thinking level (reasoning effort) for each agent CLI used by 'Run Card with AI' and the AI board loop. A second, independent axis of model selection: it says how hard the agent should think, not which model runs. Levels are CLI-specific and are passed through unchanged, so spell each one the way that CLI accepts it. A card's own `thinkingLevel.<provider>` wins, then `#mwnn-kanban.agentCliStageThinkingLevels#`, then this setting, then whatever effort that CLI runs at by default. Copilot CLI accepts `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`; OpenAI Codex CLI accepts `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, or `high`; Claude Code CLI accepts `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`. Cursor Agent CLI does not accept an effort argument; a level set for it is reported on the card and the run proceeds at its default effort without failing. Each CLI takes one level, or a list whose first entry is the level used and whose other entries are offered as suggestions in the card's thinking field. `MWNN Kanban: Populate Agent CLI Models and Thinking Levels` can fill this from the installed CLIs. Leave a CLI out for unchanged behavior.

copilot.description: Thinking level for GitHub Copilot CLI, as it spells it. Copilot accepts this value through `--effort` (also known as `--reasoning-effort`).

codex.description: Thinking level for OpenAI Codex CLI, as it spells it - for example `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, or `high`. Passed through as the `model_reasoning_effort` config override.

claude-code.description: Thinking level for Anthropic Claude Code CLI, as it spells it. Claude Code accepts this value through `--effort`.

cursor.description: Thinking level for Cursor Agent CLI, as it spells it. Cursor Agent CLI exposes no reasoning-effort argument today, so a level set here is reported as not applied and the run uses that CLI's default effort.

mwnn-kanban.agentCliStageThinkingLevels.markdownDescription: Thinking level to use for each AI board loop stage, overriding `#mwnn-kanban.agentCliThinkingLevels#` for that stage only. Useful when the short reasoning stages need less effort than the stage that does the work. The level a card names for the active CLI still wins, then this setting, then `#mwnn-kanban.agentCliThinkingLevels#` for the active CLI, then that CLI's own default effort. Levels are CLI-specific and are passed through unchanged. Leave a stage out to fall back to the workspace default; leave the whole setting empty for unchanged behavior.

definition.description: Thinking level for the definition stage, which fills in a card's Description and acceptance criteria. A short reasoning task that does not edit the workspace.

triage.description: Thinking level for the triage stage, which decides whether a card is doable as written. A short reasoning task that does not edit the workspace.

implementation.description: Thinking level for the implementation stage, which does the card's actual work in the workspace. Also used by the Run Card with AI command.

verification.description: Thinking level for the verification stage, which checks a finished card's acceptance evidence against the workspace.

mwnn-kanban.defaultColumns.description: Column titles used when a board is first created or reset. Roles are inferred from these titles, and the default set includes a Ready column for reverse-WIP tracking.

mwnn-kanban-pro.polar.organizationId.description: Polar organization id used to validate MWNN Kanban Pro license keys.

mwnn-kanban-pro.polar.benefitId.description: Polar License Keys benefit id required for MWNN Kanban Pro license validation. Leave empty only for sandbox testing without a configured benefit.

mwnn-kanban-pro.polar.apiBaseUrl.description: Polar API base URL used for MWNN Kanban Pro license validation. Change this only when testing against a Polar sandbox.

mwnn-kanban-pro.idleTimeoutMinutes.description: Minutes without tracked activity before an automatic session closes.

mwnn-kanban-pro.minSessionMinutes.description: Minimum duration in minutes for a tracked session to be persisted.

mwnn-kanban-pro.maxSliceMinutes.description: Maximum minutes in one persisted time slice before a checkpoint is written.

mwnn-kanban-pro.trackWhenUnfocused.description: Continue automatic activity tracking while the VS Code window is unfocused.

mwnn-kanban-pro.manualTimerSuppressesAut.description: Suppress automatic slices while a manual timer is running.

mwnn-kanban-pro.autoRegisterProjects.description: Automatically register workspace projects that contain a Kanban board.

mwnn-kanban-pro.projectRoots.description: Machine-local roots to scan for Kanban projects.

mwnn-kanban-pro.scanDepth.description: Maximum directory depth when scanning configured project roots.

mwnn-kanban-pro.scanIgnore.description: Machine-local directory names or paths to skip during project scans.

mwnn-kanban-pro.allocationWindowDays.description: Number of days included in allocation and drift calculations.

mwnn-kanban-pro.minTrackedHoursForDrift.description: Minimum tracked hours required before drift and debt are considered reliable.

mwnn-kanban-pro.outputWindowDays.description: Number of days included in Output and throughput calculations.

mwnn-kanban-pro.focusSessionMinutes.description: Length in minutes of a focus session.

mwnn-kanban-pro.focusBreakMinutes.description: Length in minutes of the break offered after a focus session.

mwnn-kanban-pro.driftNudges.description: Show occasional nudges when allocation drift is actionable.

mwnn-kanban-pro.nudgeThresholdPercent.description: Absolute drift percentage-point threshold before a nudge can appear.

mwnn-kanban-pro.nudgeCooldownHours.description: Minimum hours between allocation drift nudges.

mwnn-kanban-pro.showCardTrackedHours.description: Show observed tracked hours on board cards. Cards with no tracked time show nothing rather than 0h.

mwnn-kanban-pro.queueDepth.description: Maximum number of cards shown in the unified My Work queue.

mwnn-kanban-pro.backfillFromActivity.description: Include eligible historical card activity when building flow metrics.
